title: Symbiosis: A Human–AI Co-Reflection Architecture Using Graph–Vector Memory for Long-Horizon Thinking
description: Symbiosis presents a human–AI co-reflection architecture that couples large language models with a hybrid memory substrate—Neo4j for knowledge graphs, Qdrant for vector search—and a unified API with structured reflection/logging. The system is designed to enable persistent, traceable, and metacognitively informed long-horizon reasoning, demonstrated through multi-year Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) research use.

key_results.main_finding: Introduces and operationalizes a hybrid graph–vector memory architecture with structured reflection/logging that supports persistent, traceable human–AI co-reasoning over long time scales, demonstrated on multi-year EFC research.
datasets_used: Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) research materials and long-horizon dialogues (descriptive)

kill_criteria: KC1: Inability to reconstruct full provenance (source documents/conversations and transformation steps) for any stored hypothesis node from graph + logs across a multi-month window.

KC2: Hybrid retrieval (graph + vector) shows no measurable improvement over a vector-only baseline on a predefined relevance benchmark for project queries (e.g., equal or worse recall/precision across the benchmark).
KC3: Failure to replay a logged reasoning episode end-to-end with consistent retrieved context snapshots and stable summaries upon rerun, indicating inadequate reflection/logging integrity.
KC4: Missing or broken temporal linkage (e.g., updated_at, derived_from) for ≥10% of hypothesis edits over a quarter, preventing traceable evolution of ideas.
KC5: Inability to export and independently inspect the complete state (graph, embeddings, logs) using external tools, violating the inspectability/reproducibility goal.
KC6: The system autonomously forms or modifies goals without explicit human prompts or approval, violating the human-centered control constraint.
summary: This paper presents Symbiosis, a human--AI co-reflection architecture designed to support long-horizon thinking, traceable theory development, and structured cognitive work across extended timescales.
